title: VIX
body:
The **VIX** is a market-based measure of expected volatility in US equities over the next 30
days, derived from the prices of options. It is commonly described as a fear gauge.

The distinction from [[Volatility]] as computed in the dashboard is the useful part:

```
realised volatility    computed from past returns, backward looking
the VIX                implied by option prices, forward looking
```

Options are insurance against price moves, so their prices rise when buyers expect large moves,
and the VIX extracts that expectation. It measures what the market believes is coming, where
realised volatility measures what already happened.

It spikes during crises and settles during calm periods, and it rises more sharply on the way
down than on the way up, which is what makes it read as fear and not merely as uncertainty.
That asymmetry connects it to [[Investor Sentiment]]: the measure moves with the emotion
rather than only with the expected magnitude.
